name: a migration with no production-sized test evidence
why: The case the whole assessment boundary exists for. The change is eligible - it built, it passed, the container traces to the commit - and it is still not a good idea to ship yet. Waiting names the consequence, what could not be confirmed, and what the configured analysis would not catch.

observations.statement: The change alters how the service writes to its database, and the migration runs during start-up of the new version.

hazards.name: partial schema migration
preconditions: the migration runs during start-up of the new version
hazards.consequence: The stable version cannot read the rows that were already migrated, so rolling back does not restore service.

coverage.explanation: The configured analysis measures request success rate. A migration that completes but leaves rows unreadable would not appear there.

assessment.rationale: The migration's blast radius is not bounded by the configured analysis.
assessment.concern: This change alters how the service writes to its database, and the migration runs during start-up of the new version. If it fails part-way, the stable version cannot read the rows that were already migrated.
assessment.unconfirmed: Whether the migration has been run against production-sized data.
assessment.analysis_blindspot: Your configured analysis measures request success rate. A migration that completes but leaves rows unreadable would not appear there.
assessment.next_step: Run the migration as a separate job before this release, or tell me it already ran and I will reassess.
